context.title: Global Electricity Access Executive Monitor
context.goal: Track and evaluate global and regional access to electricity between 2000 and 2019, contrasting urban and rural electrification and monitoring unserved populations.
context.audience: Global development analysts, policy makers, and executive leadership

datasets.summary: Country-level annual electricity access metrics across 20 countries from 2000 to 2019, including total access percentage, urban access percentage, rural access percentage, and population without electricity access.

kpis.name: Average Electricity Access Rate
kpis.description: Mean percentage of population with access to electricity across reported countries and years.

kpis.name: Average Urban Electricity Access
kpis.description: Mean percentage of urban population with electricity access across selected regions.

kpis.name: Average Rural Electricity Access
kpis.description: Mean percentage of rural population with electricity access across selected regions.

kpis.name: Total Population Without Access
kpis.description: Total count of people lacking access to electricity across the selected countries and period.

thresholds.name: Universal Access Benchmark
thresholds.description: Indicates near-universal access to electricity at or above 90%.

thresholds.name: Critical Access Deficit
thresholds.description: Highlights regions or countries where less than half the population has electricity access.

glossary.definition: The proportion of the total national population with electricity connectivity.
The proportion of the urban population having access to electricity.
The proportion of the rural population having access to electricity.
The absolute count of individuals residing in areas without grid or reliable electricity access.

sections.title: Executive Electrification Summary
sections.purpose: Provide leadership with high-level outcome metrics, headline electrification rates, and the global deficit scale across tracked regions.

questions.text: What is the global average electricity access rate across monitored years and how does it benchmark against targets?
questions.rationale: Establishes baseline performance against the universal access benchmark for senior stakeholders.

questions.text: How many total individuals currently lack access to electricity across all monitored countries?
questions.rationale: Quantifies the aggregate unserved population to gauge total humanitarian and infrastructure scale.

questions.text: How do overall electricity access rates vary by geographic region and country?
questions.rationale: Identifies high-performing territories versus regions facing severe deficits.

sections.title: Electrification Trajectory & National Benchmarks
sections.purpose: Analyze multi-year historical trends from 2000 to 2019 to evaluate progress and speed of expansion by country.

questions.text: How has average electricity access evolved year over year from 2000 to 2019?
questions.rationale: Highlights macro progress trajectories and inflection periods in worldwide grid expansion.

questions.text: Which countries have demonstrated the steepest multi-year improvements in electricity connectivity?
questions.rationale: Showcases leading national transformation success stories such as Morocco or the Philippines.

questions.text: How has the total population without access shifted over time as national access rates climbed?
questions.rationale: Evaluates whether population growth has offset gains in electrification rates.

sections.title: Urban vs Rural Disparity & Critical Gaps
sections.purpose: Investigate structural divides between urban and rural populations to direct targeted infrastructure investments.

questions.text: What is the gap between urban electricity access and rural electricity access across regions?
questions.rationale: Pinpoints systemic electrification disparities between urbanized centers and rural communities.

questions.text: Which regions suffer from critical access shortfalls where rural access remains beneath 50%?
questions.rationale: Identifies urgent priority zones needing decentralized or off-grid energy interventions.

questions.text: Where is the largest concentration of people without electricity access located geographically?
questions.rationale: Focuses policy resources and capital deployment where deficit volume is most severe.
